chapter: Blues, cabarets and the Golden Room
title: The band at the Golden Room with cousin Mitchell Frazier
summary: Barnes names his cousin Frazier and the Golden Room band; the talk turns to the quiet neighborhood around it.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Well I think so, pretty much. We used to fight the blues, but from what I could understand, we were the best blues player. I had me, and my cousin Mitchell Frazier. I had a mic on drums, he's dead. Wouldn't you on climbing? Oh no. Something. I was on climbing.
What band was that? What was the name of that band?
Well that band then was the Golden Room. I didn't know that band then.

Who was the manager of the Golden Room? Oh, that's me. You were the manager of the Golden Room. That was Blackford Frederico. Crabby and Franklin there. Crabby and Franklin, that was a nice quiet neighborhood, huh?
Nice and quiet. Nothing much went on there.
No. We never find nothing wrong with it.
